Developer Documentation

This index identifies the current owner for each kind of maintainer-facing information. Canonical documents define project-wide policy, while focused contracts describe one subsystem without superseding their canonical parent.

Canonical project-wide sources

Area Current owner
Architecture, module ownership, and dependency direction Architecture
Repository paths and build ownership Repository Layout, with repository_structure_baseline.json as the machine-readable structural contract
Code-health and refactoring policy Code Health
Maintainer operations and recovery Maintainer Runbook
Build and dependency workflows Build and Dependency Guide
Dependency maintenance policy and quarterly review Dependency Management
Packaging and platform integration Packaging
CI and release workflow architecture GitHub Actions workflow architecture, with Main branch protection as the focused ruleset contract
Versioning and release/change-history policy Versioning Policy
Localization Localization, with the Localization glossary as its terminology companion
Documentation organization Documentation Policy

The repository tree is a navigation aid, not a second architecture or repository-layout specification.

Active subsystem and technical contracts

  • MVR: the Canonical MVR contract owns format and behavior rules. MVR identity recovery, grouped transform mutation, attachment paths, and the MVR technical-note entry points cover narrower implementation responsibilities.
  • GDTF: GDTF Mutation Policy and GDTF resource identity own write and derivative identity rules. GDTF Share catalog ingestion and the GDTF technical-note entry points cover focused catalog, compatibility, and editor behavior.
  • Application and GUI: Startup Architecture, GUI Shortcut Architecture, Storage Policy, and Text-to-scene Rules.
  • Command line: perastage-cli ships experimentally with Perastage 1.7.0 packages as a separate headless executable. The Developer CLI owns its grammar and technical contract. The Rust MCP adapter remains separately configured and is not packaged with Perastage.
  • Semantic commands: the Command API contract owns typed requests, results, headless execution context, transactional mutation, and versioned machine output independently of the current Console grammar.
  • Rendering and placement: Viewer coordinate and placement, UI unit systems, and the viewer technical-note entry points.
  • Testing and other focused policies: Test fixture policy, PDF portability, fixture category, and the remaining topic-specific documents in this directory. These apply only to their named subsystem and defer project-wide ownership to the table above.

The issue triage policy remains the focused repository-maintenance contract for issue handling.
